repairs.value: One possible extension is that a just relational salvation system would need to neutralize arbitrary differences in culture, temperament, available evidence, and cognitive style. Two equally sincere seekers could otherwise receive sharply unequal opportunities to form the required belief, even though neither controls what propositions seem convincing. On that model, belief would be a poor measure of willingness to enter relationship. Replacing torment with annihilation would not remove the concern, because permanent exclusion from an infinite good would still depend on an epistemic condition the person could not voluntarily produce.

One possible extension is to compare hiddenness with a world in which God's existence is ordinarily well supported without being absolutely certain. Inquiry, fellowship, humility, and confession could continue there through science, moral repair, vulnerability, and exploration, while different valuable conversations replaced debates caused by divine absence. Hiddenness would therefore need to supply some distinctive good that those alternatives could not preserve, and that good would need to outweigh the lost relationship suffered by sincere nonbelievers. This comparison avoids treating complete certainty as the only alternative and makes the tradeoff more precise and publicly assessable.
